empires.name: The Caliphate
empires.note: The richest trade cities on the chart, ringed by desert that starves an army before it arrives. Their coin buys assassins, and their camels make your horses bolt.

places.name: Baghdad
places.note: The throne. Round walls, four gates, and a treasury deep enough to hire whoever you just beat.

places.name: Dimashq
places.note: The good steel comes from here, and the orchards outside the wall mean no siege ever starves it.

places.name: Al-Basrah
places.note: Every cargo out of the east is stacked in these warehouses; the reed marsh around it eats horses.

places.name: Makkah
places.note: Pilgrim caravans arrive loaded. Touch it and every tribe between here and the sea rides at you.

places.name: Al-Madinah
places.note: Date groves and mudbrick, grain in cellars, and they already know the only well you can camp on.

places.name: Al-Kufah
places.note: Garrison town, half in revolt against Baghdad in any given year.

places.name: Halab
places.note: Caravans unload under a citadel on bare rock - the climb is the whole fight.

places.name: Al-Quds
places.note: Pilgrims and moneychangers behind a ridge wall, with no water outside it for you.

places.name: Hit
places.note: Bitumen wells. They boil pitch here, and pour it on whatever comes up the ladder.

empires.name: The Persian Empire
empires.note: The Immortals - kill ten thousand and ten thousand stand in the same line by morning. Satraps feed the war from provinces you have not reached, and the Royal Road brings their army to your border before your scouts get home.

places.name: Persepolis
places.note: The throne. Terraces cut into the mountainside, one ramp up, and the treasury behind all of it.

places.name: Susa
places.note: West end of the Royal Road; the plain is flat and hot and the couriers leave before you are in sight.

places.name: Ecbatana
places.note: The summer court, ringed by walls in the high Zagros, and snow shuts the passes half the year.

places.name: Marv
places.note: An oasis in dead sand. You arrive thirsty and their horse archers are already fed and mounted.

places.name: Pasargadae
places.note: The old capital: small garrison, more buried gold than most walled cities hold.

places.name: Rhagae
places.note: Where the road forks north and east - whoever holds it hears about you first.

places.name: Gabae
places.note: River town in the middle of everything, with remounts and fodder for any army passing through.

places.name: Nishapur
places.note: Turquoise mines in the hills above; the town itself has no wall worth the name.

places.name: Zarang
places.note: Mudbrick at the edge of a marsh, in a wind that blows four months without stopping.
